newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM's party head says no threat to government.
newsitem.headline: India PM's party head says no threat to government.

text.p: The beleaguered chief of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party stressed on Friday that an impending split within the group would not endanger the survival of the two-month-old government.

"There is no danger to the government. If the prime minister is ever in trouble, then Laloo Yadav will be the first to jump up and help him," Janata Dal party president Laloo Prasad Yadav told reporters.
Yadav said he would meet Gujral later on Friday, ahead of a convention scheduled for Saturday at which Yadav's supporters are expected to announce the formation of a splinter group.

Federal police have indicted Yadav and 55 others in a $280 million embezzlement scandal over animal welfare funds. He says he is innocent and has repeatedly rejected calls from other partners of the coalition that he resign.

Friday's meeting was seen as a last-ditch effort by the prime minister to patch over a rift within his deeply divided party, which was forced to hold internal elections for the first time in nine years on Thursday.
The government on Monday removed the head of India's federal police who had spearheaded the probe into the animal fodder scandal.
Yadav's supporters said the voters' lists were rigged to favour his rival and said they would hold a parallel election.

Yadav, a popular low-caste leader who is also chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, said he had the support of 24 Janata Dal lawmakers out of 45. The party is the largest group in the ruling centre-left United Front alliance.

The president of the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Lal Krishna Advani, predicted the Congress party would soon launch a bid for power, just months after it toppled a previous United Front government by abruptly withdrawing support.

"I can foresee Congress making yet another bid to grab power in Delhi no sooner than there is a split in the Janata Dal. Last time they tried it in April but failed and decided to let the United Front continue," Advani told reporters in the northern city of Lucknow.
Gujral's minority government depends on Congress to survive in parliament, where the BJP holds the most seats but short of a majority.

"The instability of the central government in Delhi is largely on account of the incongruous arrangement between them and Congress. Despite being the larger party, Congress is extending support to it from outside," he said.
News reports quoted Congress leaders exhorting party cadres to prepare for mid-term polls.
